attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-member MariaDB 10.5 Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, AlmaLinux 9.6) using mariadb-server-galera + galera + mariadb-backup. Fixed two environment issues along the way: wsrep_provider path (galera-4 -> galera) and an SELinux AVC denial blocking mariabackup's connectto on the mysqld unix socket (resolved with a scoped semodule policy allowing mysqld_t->mysqld_t unix_stream_socket connectto). Firewall ports 3306/4567/4568/4444 opened on all nodes. Verified multi-master write propagation (writes from any node visible on the others), availability during a single-node outage (2/3 quorum, writes continued), and automatic resync of the rejoining node (SST/IST caught it up to full row set, wsrep_local_state=Synced). Completed mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node1, node2, then node3 sequentially (one at a time, quorum preserved throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each rejoined with wsrep_cluster_size=3, state=Synced, wsrep_ready=ON, and full data (5/5 rows) after each restart. Final state: all 3 nodes synced, cluster_size=3, data consistent everywhere. Credentials (SST user password, appuser password) were generated on-node and passed only via secret_env, never printed after initial generation.
